name: H-1B Specialty Occupation Visa

selection_odds.basis: Wage-weighted lottery from Feb 27, 2026 (DHS final rule, effective for FY2027 cap): each unique beneficiary entered multiple times by OEWS prevailing-wage level — Level IV=4 entries, Level III=3, Level II=2, Level I=1. Replaces the pure random lottery used through FY2026.

application_window.note: FY2027 registration window; petitions filed April 1 - June 30, 2026

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a specialty occupation role requiring at least a bachelor's degree or equivalent, and selection in the cap lottery: 65,000 regular cap + 20,000 US-advanced-degree exemption, unless the employer is cap-exempt (higher-education institutions and affiliated nonprofits, nonprofit research organizations, governmental research organizations).
requirements.fix_path: Secure a specialty-occupation job offer and be selected in the registration lottery, or find a cap-exempt employer.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires the employer to pay the higher of the DOL-certified prevailing wage (four-level OEWS system) or the actual wage paid to similarly employed workers.

A $100,000 fee (Presidential Proclamation, effective Sept 21, 2025) applies to new H-1B petitions for beneficiaries outside the US who don't already hold a valid H-1B visa, or petitions requesting consular/port-of-entry notification. Change of status from F-1 while inside the US is exempt.

evidence_required.document: Labor Condition Application (LCA) certified by DOL

outcome.duration_length: 3 years, extendable to 6 (beyond 6 with an approved I-140, or if PERM/I-140 has been pending 365+ days)

sources.title: Federal Register - Weighted Selection Process for H-1B Registrants, Dec 29, 2025 (doc 2025-23853)
USCIS guidance on Presidential Proclamation restricting entry of certain nonimmigrant workers, Oct 20, 2025

notes: MAJOR STRUCTURAL CHANGE confirmed and in force: the H-1B selection moved from a pure random lottery to a wage-weighted lottery (DHS final rule, effective Feb 27, 2026, first used FY2027) — higher-wage-level job offers get proportionally more chances in the pool. selection_method changed from 'lottery' in spirit to a weighted variant; encoded here as 'lottery' with the weighting mechanic captured in selection_odds since the schema's selection_method enum doesn't have a dedicated weighted-lottery value — a minor schema-fit gap worth flagging. The $100,000 proclamation fee is modeled as a soft (non-hard) requirement since it's a cost condition rather than an eligibility gate, and its scope is genuinely narrow (excludes change-of-status, extensions, and previously-issued valid visas) — many secondary sources overstate its reach. Registration fee $215/beneficiary (non-refundable), confirmed for FY2027. pr_after_months/citizenship_after_months left null since these depend entirely on the underlying employment-based category and country of birth (see us_eb1/eb2/eb3's severe India/China backlogs) — a single figure would be misleading.
